summary: Clackamas County site east of Estacada: women staffed a station here in 1918, a wooden L-4 tower stood from 1933, it was gone by 1967, and an August 2026 notice closes the area.

facts.design: Wooden L-4 tower (1933, per register); a 1947 survey describes a one-room building on poles
facts.status_note: Tower gone by 1967; the summit is the site of a former lookout
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Mount Hood National Forest

access.note: Oregon Hikers notice dated August 2026 says the area is closed because of the Austin Fire; the Forest Service closure order was not read

visit.trail_note: About 8.1 miles round trip from the Fish Creek Mountain trailhead; burned by the 2020 Riverside Fire; flagged as a lost hike

events.note: Two women in charge of the station; Mrs. Anna Morton named as lookout in September
Tent with firefinder and telephone on the summit, around 1925 (register)
Wooden L-4 tower replaced the tent
September 1963 inspection: rotting legs, cracked footings; recommended replacement
Gone by 1967 per the register and Firelookout.com
Registered August 24, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek
Riverside Fire burned the area intensely
Area closed because of the Austin Fire (notice dated August 2026)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Firelookout.com give the 1933 tower as 12 feet; the 1947 survey says about 30 feet. The record's 9.1 m (30 ft) follows the survey; the disagreement is left open.
The register dates the tent to around 1925, but newspaper reports quoted by the Forest Lookouts page show women in charge of the station in 1918, so the station predates the register's date.

notes_for_editor: Height is disputed (12 ft in the register and Firelookout.com, about 30 ft in the 1947 survey). The closure notice is taken from the Oregon Hikers page and was not checked against the Forest Service closure order, which was not read. The newspaper quotes come from a transcription on the Forest Lookouts page, not the original papers. The Trail Advocates Fish Creek page and the Oregon Hikers post-fire report were not read.
